page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, consisting of 1 physical core with 2 threads. The instance is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1.0 GB per core allocation. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25% due to the low core count. Memory bandwidth is limited, with read-only large block bandwidth at 29.49 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 21.35 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 25%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance.

This instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-focused workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but have minimal memory requirements. Due to the low memory capacity and poor database operations benchmark score, it is not suited for memory-intensive applications or database hosting. It is best utilized for lightweight single-threaded processing, basic web serving, or simple background tasks.
